guide.summary: Easy to start. For your own workspace, an internal connection token needs no OAuth at all. Composio's managed Notion app covers prototypes. Your own public OAuth connection takes under an hour to set up and needs no scopes, only capabilities. Notion's docs contradict each other on whether the Authorization URL needs a review submission first. The only clearly documented review (5-10 business days) is for an optional Marketplace listing.

composio.note: The NOTION toolkit supports OAUTH2 (Composio-managed app available) and API_KEY (internal connection token). With the managed app, users see 'Composio' as the connection, and tokens are shared across Composio customers, so Composio recommends your own app for production. A separate NOTION_MCP toolkit uses DCR_OAUTH, has no managed app, and is listed under 'Bring your own OAuth app'. Notion's MCP server supports dynamic client registration. Composio's credential guide still describes the older notion.so/profile/integrations UI; copy the callback URI from your Composio dashboard, not from that guide.

need_own_app.answer: Not to prototype: Composio's managed Notion app works. For one workspace you own, skip OAuth and use an internal token. For other people's workspaces, use your own public connection.
reasons: Branding: Notion attributes actions and the connection name to the integration, so with the managed app users see 'Composio'.
Token isolation: with a shared app, a user reconnecting elsewhere through the same app can invalidate your older refresh token.
Webhook triggers on your own client ID need your own app and a manual verification step.
Marketplace listing requires your own 'Any workspace' public connection.
Enterprise admins approve connections by name; your own connection name is easier to justify than 'Composio'.

scenarios.label: Prototype on Composio's managed app
scenarios.when_this_applies: You are building or demoing, and users can accept seeing 'Composio' as the connection name in their Notion workspace.

hands_on.basis: No Notion app to create; only a Composio auth config (c28, c31). Estimate from step count, not measured.

scenarios.approval: None from Notion for you. Users still pick pages at consent (c19).

scenarios.label: Internal connection, your own workspace
scenarios.when_this_applies: The agent only touches one workspace you own or administer, e.g. your team's own automation. Use Composio's API_KEY auth with the internal connection token.

hands_on.basis: Create connection, copy token, share pages, create Composio API-key auth config (c2, c3, c4). Estimate from step count, not measured.

waiting.basis: Token is issued immediately at creation (c3).

scenarios.approval: None. Requires Workspace Owner role in that workspace (c2).

scenarios.label: Public connection, not listed
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your users connect their own Notion workspaces through Composio and you want your own name/logo, isolated tokens, or your own webhooks. You do not need Marketplace discovery.

hands_on.basis: Create public connection, set redirect URI, scope, capabilities; copy client ID/secret into Composio; test with a second workspace (c7, c8). Estimate from step count, not measured.

waiting.basis: Official docs say a public connection works via OAuth without a Marketplace listing (c12, c13). But the authorization guide's caption says the Authorization URL populates only after the connection is 'submitted for review' (c9). The older wording suggests no review gate (c11). Not confirmed (c44).

scenarios.approval: No documented approval for an unlisted public connection, apart from the ambiguous 'submitted for review' caption. Enterprise workspaces may block installs (c24).

scenarios.label: Listed on the Notion Marketplace
scenarios.when_this_applies: You want your connection discoverable in Notion's Marketplace. Requires an 'Any workspace' public connection.

hands_on.basis: Listing copy, category/tags, images and logo, plus everything in s3 (c17). Estimate from step count, not measured.

waiting.estimate: 5-10 business days to first response, per submission
waiting.basis: Notion's Marketplace FAQ (c15). Rejections add another cycle (c16).

scenarios.approval: Notion team review / security review of the listing (c13, c15, c16).

prerequisites.title: A Notion account and a workspace where you are Workspace Owner
prerequisites.detail: Needed to create internal connections; public connections need a development workspace.

prerequisites.title: Composio account and the callback URI from its dashboard
prerequisites.detail: Used as the redirect URI on the public connection.

prerequisites.title: Website, privacy policy, terms of use, support email and icon
prerequisites.detail: Older Notion public-integration forms required these. Current official docs don't list them for the connection, so treat them as possibly required.

prerequisites.title: A second Notion workspace for testing
prerequisites.detail: Needed to confirm OAuth works outside your development workspace (each user authorizes individually).

steps.title: Pick the path: managed app, internal token, or your own public connection
steps.detail: An agent can map your use case to a scenario. One workspace you own: internal connection (s2). Other people's workspaces with your branding or isolated tokens: public connection (s3). Discovery: Marketplace (s4). If you choose public, decide Any workspace vs Selected workspaces only now, because it is permanent and only Any workspace can be listed.
inputs: Who will connect (you only, known customers, anyone)
steps.done_when: Scenario and installation scope are chosen.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config using Composio's managed Notion app
steps.detail: In the Composio dashboard, create a Notion auth config with Composio-managed OAuth. No scopes are needed. Users will see 'Composio' as the connection.
steps.done_when: Auth config ID (ac_...) exists and a test user can connect and pick pages.

steps.title: Create an internal connection and copy its token
steps.detail: Developer portal > Build > Internal connections > Create a new connection. Choose the workspace and set capabilities on the Configuration tab. Copy the API token from that tab and store it in a secret manager.
inputs: Workspace Owner role in the target workspace
steps.done_when: You have the internal connection API token.

steps.title: Share pages with the internal connection
steps.detail: Content access tab > Edit access, or on a page use ••• > Connections > Add connection. Sharing a parent page shares its children. Without this step every API call errors.
inputs: List of pages/databases the agent needs
steps.done_when: A test API call (e.g. search) returns the shared pages.

steps.title: Create a Composio API-key auth config with the internal token
steps.detail: In Composio, create a Notion auth config with API Key auth and supply the internal connection token. No OAuth redirect is involved.
steps.done_when: Composio connected account works in the Playground or a test tool call.

steps.title: Choose minimum capabilities
steps.detail: Notion uses capabilities (read/update/insert content, read/insert comments, user info with or without email), not OAuth scopes. An agent can map the Composio tools you plan to use to the minimum capability set. Changing capabilities later forces every user to re-authenticate.
inputs: List of Composio Notion tools your agent will call
steps.done_when: A capability list is written down with a reason for each.

steps.title: Copy the redirect/callback URI from your Composio dashboard
steps.detail: Create (or start creating) a Notion auth config with 'use your own developer credentials' and copy the callback URI Composio shows. Do not copy one from a blog post; Composio's own docs show more than one.
steps.done_when: You have the exact callback URI string.

steps.title: Create the public connection in the Notion Developer portal
steps.detail: Developer portal > Build > Public connections > Create new connection. Enter name, development workspace, the Composio redirect URI, installation scope (Any workspace or Selected workspaces only; permanent) and capabilities. If the portal asks for website, privacy policy, terms or support email, have them ready (older forms did; current docs don't say).
inputs: Possibly: website, privacy policy URL, terms URL, support email, icon
steps.done_when: Connection exists and the Configuration tab shows an OAuth client ID and secret.

steps.title: Check whether the Authorization URL field is populated
steps.detail: Notion's guide says the Authorization URL field populates after the connection is 'submitted for review'. Composio builds its own authorize URL from your client ID, so you may not need this field. If it is empty, test OAuth anyway (next steps) before assuming a review is required.
inputs: Access to the connection's Configuration tab
steps.done_when: You know whether the field is filled, and whether a test OAuth from a second workspace succeeds.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config with your own client ID/secret
steps.detail: In Composio, create a Notion OAuth2 auth config with your own developer credentials. Paste the client ID and secret. No scopes are needed.
steps.done_when: Auth config ID (ac_...) saved in your secret manager.

steps.title: Test OAuth from a workspace that is not your development workspace
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection as a test user in a second Notion workspace. Pick pages in the picker and confirm the redirect returns to Composio and a tool call can read the picked pages. This is the real check on the review-gate question.
inputs: A second Notion workspace (free is fine)
steps.done_when: Connected account is ACTIVE and a read tool returns a picked page.

steps.title: Set up webhooks for triggers (own app only)
steps.detail: If you use Composio Notion triggers with your own app, create a Composio webhook endpoint for your client ID, paste the webhook_url into Notion's webhook settings, then read the verification token from Composio and paste it back into Notion. An agent can run the API calls; you paste the values into the Notion UI.
steps.done_when: Notion shows the webhook as verified.

steps.title: Draft the Marketplace listing
steps.detail: An agent can draft the listing name, description, category and tags, and a checklist of images/logo. It can also check that the listing avoids trademark problems with Notion's brand.
steps.done_when: Draft listing text and assets are ready.

steps.title: Create and submit the listing
steps.detail: Marketplace listing dashboard > Listings > Connections > Start a new connection listing. Fill in details, associate the 'Any workspace' public connection, save draft, then submit for review.

steps.title: Wait for Notion's review
steps.detail: Notion replies by email, typically within 5-10 business days. If rejected, fix the feedback and resubmit.
steps.done_when: Listing approved and visible in the Notion Marketplace.

traps.title: Installation scope is permanent
traps.detail: Picking 'Selected workspaces only' rules out the Marketplace forever; you would have to create a new connection, and every user would reconnect.

traps.title: Changing capabilities forces re-auth
traps.detail: Adding a capability later makes every existing user re-authenticate, so choose carefully up front.

traps.title: Refresh tokens rotate
traps.detail: Every refresh returns a new refresh token, and reconnecting the same user can invalidate the old one. Keep one connection per user per app.

traps.title: No page access means empty results, not an auth error at connect time
traps.detail: Internal connections start with zero pages. OAuth users only grant the pages they pick, and only pages they have full access to.

traps.title: One user's OAuth does not cover the team
traps.detail: Each workspace member must authorize the public connection separately; tokens act for that user.

traps.title: PATs are off by default on Business/Enterprise
traps.detail: Don't plan on personal access tokens for customer workspaces; owners must enable them.

traps.title: redirect_uri in token exchange
traps.detail: Usually required, but not allowed when there is one redirect URI and the authorize URL omitted it. Composio handles this, but it matters if you test by hand.

blockers.symptom: Authorization URL field on the Configuration tab is empty
blockers.what_it_means: Notion's guide says it populates after the connection is 'submitted for review'. Older docs said only 'submitted' (the public form). It may just mean the public setup isn't saved.
blockers.what_to_do: Use Composio, which builds the authorize URL from your client ID, and test from a second workspace. If the install page errors, look for a submit/publish action in the Developer portal or contact Notion developer support.
blockers.agent_can_help: Build the authorize URL from your client ID and redirect URI, and diagnose the redirect result.

blockers.symptom: User can't find or install your connection in an Enterprise workspace
blockers.what_it_means: Workspace owners on Enterprise can restrict which connections members may install.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the workspace owner to allow it. Request minimal capabilities to make approval easier.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the admin request explaining capabilities and data use.

blockers.what_it_means: Brand/trademark, quality, or baseline criteria not met.
blockers.what_to_do: Read the emailed feedback, fix, resubmit; expect another 5-10 business days.
blockers.agent_can_help: Rewrite listing copy against the feedback.

blockers.symptom: API calls return errors / search returns nothing after connecting
blockers.what_it_means: The connection has no access to those pages.
blockers.what_to_do: Internal: share pages via Content access or Add connections. Public: have the user reconnect and pick the pages, or add the connection to pages in Notion.
blockers.agent_can_help: List what the token can see (search) and tell the user which pages to share.

open_questions: Does a public connection created in the new Developer portal complete OAuth for other workspaces before any Notion review? Docs conflict (authorization-guide caption vs Marketplace FAQ). Find out by creating one and connecting from a second workspace through Composio.
Does the new Developer portal require website / privacy policy / terms / support email on the public connection itself, or only on the Marketplace listing? Find out by creating a public connection.
Does Composio's NOTION API_KEY auth accept a personal access token, not just an internal connection token? Test with a PAT.
For NOTION_MCP (DCR_OAUTH), does Composio register a client automatically or ask for credentials? Check by creating an auth config in the Composio dashboard.

claims.text: Notion's documented credential types are internal connections (static workspace API token), personal access tokens (user-scoped static token), and public connections (OAuth 2.0).
claims.quote: Internal connections use a static credential called an internal connection API token, personal access tokens use a user-scoped static token, and public connections use the OAuth 2.0 protocol.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Only a Workspace Owner can create an internal connection.
claims.quote: You must be a Workspace Owner to create a connection.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: An internal connection needs no OAuth flow; its token is available immediately after creation.
claims.quote: There’s no OAuth flow to implement — you get a token immediately when you create the connection
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: A new internal connection can see no pages until pages are shared with it (Content access tab or the page's Add connections menu).
claims.quote: A newly created connection has no page access by default.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: A public connection's installation scope (Any workspace vs Selected workspaces only) is chosen at creation and cannot be changed later.
claims.quote: Installation scope is set once, at creation time, and can’t be changed afterward.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Only 'Any workspace' public connections are Marketplace-eligible; 'Selected workspaces only' connections are not.
claims.quote: either Any workspace (Marketplace-eligible) or Selected workspaces only (not Marketplace-eligible)
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Public connections are created in the Developer portal (Build > Public connections) with name, development workspace, redirect URIs, installation scope and capabilities.
claims.quote: Click Create new connection and fill in the required fields, including:
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.note: The quote shares few words with this claim. Read it before relying on the claim.

claims.text: The OAuth client ID and client secret are on the connection's Configuration tab after creation.
claims.quote: After creation, visit the Configuration tab to retrieve your OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Notion's current authorization guide captions its screenshot: the Authorization URL field populates only after a public connection is submitted for review.
claims.quote: The Authorization URL field populates after a public connection is submitted for review
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: The authorization guide says to switch code to the public auth flow once the connection has been 'made public'.
claims.quote: Once your connection has been made public, you can update your connection code to use the public auth flow.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: The 2024 version of the same guide had the same caption without 'for review' ('populates after a public integration is submitted'), meaning submitting the public-integration form. The current page reuses the same old screenshot. That suggests 'for review' was added in a rewording, not as a new review gate. This is an inference, not a confirmed fact.
claims.label: reported
claims.note: Wayback Machine copy of developers.notion.com/docs/authorization (2024). Old wording: 'The Authorization URL field populates after a public integration is submitted'.

claims.text: Marketplace listing is optional. A public connection works through its OAuth flow without being listed.
claims.quote: your connection can be used via its OAuth flow without being listed
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Notion's security review applies before a Marketplace listing; you can create and use a public connection without listing it.
claims.quote: Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Only public connections with installation scope 'Any workspace' can be listed on the Marketplace.
claims.quote: Only public connections with an installation scope of Any workspace can be listed on the Marketplace.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Notion says to expect a reply on a Marketplace submission within 5-10 business days, by email.
claims.quote: expect to hear back from our team within 5-10 business days via email
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Marketplace submissions can be rejected for brand/trademark issues, quality, or unmet baseline criteria. You can fix them and resubmit.
claims.quote: Connections are rejected for various reasons, from brand/trademark issues to quality concerns
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Marketplace listing details (description, categories, images) are managed separately from the connection, in the Listings section.
claims.quote: Marketplace listing details (such as descriptions, categories, and images) are managed separately through the Listings section.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: The authorize endpoint is https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and owner=user.
claims.quote: The URL begins with https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize and has the following parameters:
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: At consent, users pick pages in a page picker that only shows pages they have full access to.
claims.quote: The page picker only displays pages or databases to which a user has full access
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Each workspace member who wants to use a public connection must go through OAuth individually.
claims.quote: each prospective user needs to individually follow the auth flow for the connection
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Refreshing a Notion access token returns a new access token and a new refresh token (rotation).
claims.quote: Refreshing an access token will generate a new access token and a new refresh token.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: If you change a public connection's capabilities, users must re-authenticate.
claims.quote: For public connections, users will need to re-authenticate with a connection if the capabilities are changed
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Requesting fewer capabilities makes it more likely that a workspace admin allows the install.
claims.quote: The fewer capabilities you request, the more likely a workspace admin will be able to install your connection.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: On Enterprise plans, workspace owners can restrict which connections members can install.
claims.quote: On Enterprise plans, workspace owners can restrict which connections members are allowed to install.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: If the user clicks Allow access but your code-for-token exchange fails, the connection gets no page access.
claims.quote: If the user clicks Allow access and the rest of the auth flow is not completed, the connection will not have access to the pages that were selected.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Personal access tokens act as the creating user, with no OAuth flow and no page picker.
claims.quote: There is no OAuth flow and no page picker.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: On Business and Enterprise plans, PAT creation is off until a workspace owner enables it.
claims.quote: On Business and Enterprise plans, PAT creation is restricted by default.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Composio has a managed OAuth app for the NOTION toolkit, which supports OAUTH2 and API_KEY auth.
claims.quote: Composio-managed OAuth available? Yes
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Notion shows actions as coming from the integration, so with Composio's managed app users see 'Composio', not your product.
claims.quote: Notion attributes actions to the integration itself, not the individual user.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: To show your own name and logo, create your own Notion integration.
claims.quote: To use a custom name or logo, create your own Notion integration.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Notion has no OAuth scopes; access is per page. Composio auth configs for Notion need no scopes.
claims.quote: You don't need to pass scopes when creating an auth config.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Composio recommends your own Notion app for production so users' tokens are isolated to your product. If the same user reconnects through the shared app, the older refresh token can be invalidated.
claims.quote: we strongly recommend using your own Notion app so your users' tokens are isolated to your product
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: With your own Notion OAuth app, you set up Notion webhook triggers yourself: create a Composio webhook endpoint, paste its URL into Notion, then paste the verification token back into Notion.
claims.quote: If you bring your own Notion OAuth app, the verification flow runs in reverse from Slack's
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Composio's separate NOTION_MCP toolkit uses DCR_OAUTH and has no Composio-managed OAuth app.
claims.quote: Composio-managed OAuth available? No
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Composio's rule: if a toolkit has no managed scheme for its OAuth method, register your own OAuth app.
claims.quote: If the field does not contain that method, register your own OAuth app and supply its client ID and client secret.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Notion's hosted MCP server supports dynamic client registration (RFC 7591), so an MCP client can register itself without a Developer portal app.
claims.quote: Notion MCP server supports dynamic client registration (RFC 7591).
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: GET to the authorize endpoint with client_id=invalid-client-id-test returns a 302 to app.notion.com/install-integration without rejecting the client_id at the HTTP level.
claims.label: probed

claims.text: The app.notion.com/install-integration page returns 200 with a JavaScript shell. Client ID validation (and any 'not yet available' error) happens in the browser app, so an HTTP probe cannot tell whether an unreviewed public connection's OAuth works.
claims.label: probed

claims.text: The integrations dashboard (notion.so/profile/integrations) redirects to app.notion.com and requires a Notion login.
claims.label: probed

claims.text: Notion MCP's OAuth metadata advertises a registration_endpoint (https://mcp.notion.com/register), confirming dynamic client registration.
claims.label: probed

claims.text: A third-party guide (Ampersand) lists the older public-integration form fields: Website, Privacy Policy URL, Terms of Use URL, contact Email, and an icon.
claims.label: reported

claims.text: n8n's guide describes the older flow: Distribution tab, turn on 'make this integration public', then enter company name and website.
claims.label: reported

claims.text: The current official Developer portal docs do not list website, privacy policy, terms or support email as required fields when creating a public connection. Whether the new portal still requires them (on the connection or only on the Marketplace listing) is unconfirmed.
claims.label: unknown

claims.text: Unconfirmed: whether a public connection created in the new Developer portal can complete OAuth with workspaces other than your own before any Notion review. Official docs conflict: the caption says the Authorization URL appears after submission 'for review', but the Marketplace FAQ says connections work via OAuth without a listing.
claims.label: unknown

claims.text: Unconfirmed: whether Composio's NOTION API_KEY auth accepts a personal access token as well as an internal connection token. Both are bearer tokens to Notion, but Composio's docs only name internal tokens.
claims.label: unknown

claims.text: Unconfirmed: whether Composio's DCR_OAUTH for NOTION_MCP needs any client ID/secret from you, or registers a client automatically.
claims.label: unknown

claims.text: Public connection tokens act for the authorizing user and are scoped to that user's workspace.
claims.quote: each user who authorizes the connection receives their own access token, scoped to their workspace
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: In the token exchange, redirect_uri is usually required. It is not allowed if the connection has one redirect URI and the authorize URL did not include one.
claims.quote: In most cases, the redirect_uri field is required.
claims.label: provider_docs

guide.verdict: Minutes to prototype, under an hour for your own public connection. Only an optional Marketplace listing is reviewed, in 5 to 10 business days.

meta.review_note: Researched ahead of time under the same evidence rules as the live agent. Quotes re-checked against their source pages on 20 Oct 2026. Not yet hands-on tested.
